body:
David Buchanan wrote:
> 
> WHEN DID TK BECOME AN ENVIRONMENTALIST?
> <snipped>
> 1) TK claimed to have abandoned his career because "he was tired of
> teaching engineers 'math that was going to be used for destroying the
> environment.'"  TK had spent most of his life working towards that career.
> If he abandoned an apparently promising career for environmental reasons,
> then he must have held pretty strong environmental opinions -- much
> stronger than those of the average fisherman or camper.  Is there any
> evidence that TK held such strong opinions *before* dropping out of
> Berkeley?  I haven't seen any.

I see one way you people go wrong.  You assume TK would be interested in
a "career."  The problem is, many geniuses, particularly individualistic
ones, do not think in terms of "career."  They devote their time to pure
thought, rapt in the pleasure of abstract thought and the obsession to
understand or create.  Sometimes a career is an outgrowth, sometimes it
is a rent-paying necessity, seldom is it a priority over the avocation
of thinking.  It's doubtful TK pursued "curvilinear functions" because
they represented a lucrative career.  More likely, he had an interest in
mathematics, pursued it academically, and easily fell into a "career" in
academia.  When he realized he was a tool for the system, when he felt
that his intellectual endeavors served no other purpose than to educate
a bunch of snotty, future bomb-designers-of-America, when he realized
like many 26-year-olds that he was dissatisfied with his job, he said --
as many have -- what am I doing here?  Admittedly, he had some social
inadequacies, but to attribute everything he did to them is
preposterous.

> 2) If TK was interested in saving the environment and was able to cope
> with the emotional and social aspects of his teaching job at Berkeley,
> then why didn't he stay there?  Faculty positions at prominent
> universities -- and some not so prominent ones -- have provided many
> academics with convenient platforms from which they can express their
> opinions (usually on subjects of which they are woefully ignorant).  It
> would also have given him an opportunity to recruit students to his cause.
> Finally it would have provided him with a secure and fairly adequate
> source of income to finance his bombing campaign if that was his
> intention.  If TK wanted to save the environment instead of just escape
> into it, he should have stayed at Berkeley.

Again, you presume life goals that have more to do with materialistic or
social success than with ideology and conviction.  An ideologue with
strong conviction in their beliefs, not to mention a preference for
nature over "industrial society," would very likely do exactly what TK
did.

> 3) If saving the environment was one of TK's primary motives, then why
> isn't it featured much more prominently in the Manifesto and why is
> protecting the environment completely missing from the 1971 Essay?
 
There are references to the destruction of nature by the industrial
system throughout the manifesto.  Here are the first two sentences: 
"The Industrial Revolution and its consequences have been a disaster for
the human race.  They have greatly increased the life-expectancy of
those of us who live in "advanced" countries, but they have destabilized
society, have made life unfulfilling, have subjected human beings to
indignities, have led to widespread psychological suffering (in the
Third World to physical suffering as well) and have inflicted severe
damage on the natural world."  There is actually a lot about nature in
the manifesto, but why focus on TK's motives, conscious or
subconscious?  If he were just a bomber there would be no newsgroup
devoted to him.  Is there a alt.fan.george.metesky or an
alt.fan.guy.fawkes newsgroup?  

Reading the manifesto and the letters, it does become evident TK is
nuts, but nuttiness does not invalidate the ideas in the manifesto any
more than it invalidates the work of Ezra Pound, Edgar Allen Poe or any
number of scientists/authors/artists.  As D.H. Lawrence said, "Trust the
tale, not the teller."

headers.Subject: Re: When did TK become an environmentalist?
